page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a-nps1.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by a KVM hypervisor, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at 2.55 GHz. Memory configuration comprises 256.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. Network performance is anchored by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance carries no integrated local storage or hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results place the instance in the upper performance tier for memory throughput and single-core tasks, achieving a PassMark memory score of 2760.07 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2694.49, both ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core compute performance falls within the middle 50%, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 43092.5, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 13075.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 38143.99. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 82.73 GB/s uncached read throughput and 46.95 GB/s uncached write throughput. High-throughput in-memory operations reached 30.68 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside 13335.27 operations in PassMark database testing.

Because the ecs.r7a-nps1.8xlarge does not include local disk storage, all persistent data workloads require external cloud storage volumes. Cost efficiency is driven by the dense 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, which reduces per-gigabyte overhead for memory-bound tasks without paying for unused GPU silicon or dedicated local NVMe arrays. This hardware configuration is suited for enterprise in-memory databases like Redis, medium-to-large relational database engines, real-time analytics, and heavy ETL pipelines requiring expansive system memory.
